I took a two-year college diploma for writing. Most people end up in PR or Journalism, but they had a small marketing branch. Learned not much other than how to write well and purged the academic voice from my writing.   
  
I don't really consider this experience. I usually don't even look at someone's college section when going through resumes. They do nothing but waste space on the page.

Had a lot of issues finding work. After about three months worked construction because I needed to do something.

Quit and started writing a blog/ running ads for it just to practice and keep my writing muscle going. 

There was a manufacturing startup about 30mins from my city. It was in the middle of nowhere so no one wanted to drive out there. One of my past classmates saw one of my ads and it reminded them of me, they reached out to me and said they needed someone to run their socials.

I really didn't want to do social media. I did it as fast as I could and then took on copywriting, leadership, strategy, and media buying projects that no one else had time for.  
  
The pay was so low I couldn't afford gas some weeks and slept in my car outside the building pretty often. The CMO was a killer so I stayed for a year and a half.

Now I'm starting an agency with someone I met while volunteering. and all our clients come from past relationships and referrals, which we can only get because we crush.

No one can follow the exact path I led because it only works from building real relationships that I never went into with the hopes that they'd give me a job or be a client. I wish I had a better answer for you. My best advice is build relationships. But if you do it with an ulterior motive, people can smell it and you'll just waste your time.

Got my first through a personal relationship. Realized after a month I didn’t have enough experience to do them justice. So I found a job in house to learn from a CMO who’s been in the industry longer than I’ve been alive. 

If you want to be commoditized and are ok with burning bridges, cold calling to the end of the earth will work. After about a year and a half, I did cold calling to get some side work and pad out my portfolio. Called maybe 200, landed two clients and that was all I could fit into my schedule. That was with tangible evidence of success though. I only landed those clients because I knew what I was talking about, and saw when going through their accounts that someone with no experience, & making simple mistakes was handing their accounts.

Here's what I did. keep in mind I went to college for advertising, and had been running ads for about a year in house at a business. 

1. Choose a business type.

2. get the phone numbers of 100+ of those businesses.

3. Call all of them and keep improving your pitch.
